test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A bus travel the first 60 m in 30 s and then another 80 m in 40 s. Calculate the average speed of the bus in m s⁻¹.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is calculated as the ratio of total distance covered to the total time taken.

Total Distance = 60 + 80 = 140 m

Total Time = 30 + 40 = 70 s

Average Speed = 140 ÷ 70 = 2 m s⁻¹

**∴ The correct answer is 2 m s⁻¹.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03893df475c78cf8afdfe2092869d709e8a9c941cb55ea784e4b25903dc7ffda.png] 

**Given:**

First distance (d₁) = 60 m

First time (t₁) = 30 s

Second distance (d₂) = 80 m

Second time (t₂) = 40 s

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance = d₁ + d₂

⇒ Total Distance = 60 + 80 = 140 m

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂

⇒ Total Time = 30 + 40 = 70 s

⇒ Average Speed = 140 ÷ 70

⇒ Average Speed = 2 m s⁻¹

**∴ The correct answer is 2 m s⁻¹.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a journey is divided into equal distances covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the formula (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a journey involves travelling at speeds x and y for exactly equal time intervals, the overall average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds. For objects moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds.
